title: Bahai Badi Calendar
intro: The Badi calendar is the religious solar calendar of the Bahá'í Faith.
epoch: The Bahá'í Era (B.E.) begins in 1844, linked to the declaration of the Báb. Naw-Rúz is the New Year.
structure: Nineteen months each contain nineteen days (361 days). Ayyam-i-Ha adds four or five days between months 18 and 19, bringing the year to 365 or 366 days.
example: After day 19 of Mulk comes the intercalary interval, followed by Ala 1. Month names use simple Roman-letter spellings; transliterations vary.
history: The Báb introduced the Badi calendar and Bahá'u'lláh confirmed it. Its month names reflect attributes of God.
model: The provider uses the Gregorian 21 March start in years 1–171 B.E. From 172 B.E., it computes the Tehran equinox/sunset boundary in the documented astronomical range. Outside the documented astronomical range the continuation uses 21 March.
limits: Astronomical calculations for Gregorian years 1000–3000 are approximate. Religious days begin at sunset, but the date-only day-number interface does not implement an intraday sunset rollover. A failed year-start calculation must not be represented as the 1844 epoch. The October 2026 audit matched 50 published Naw-Ruz dates (2015–2064), not every historical observance or distant prediction.
